title: Add support for math in blastula_email rmarkdown format
description:
This is a POC to test how we could support math easily in blastula rmardown fomat following the improved support in **rmarkdown** This first test is using `webtex` method which allow to use an online service to insert math as SVG (default) or PNG in HTML document. Hopefully self-contained image like SVG or PNG are ok to be included in email. Another possible method would be using the [**katex**]() R package https://docs.ropensci.org/katex/index.html that we support through `math_method: r-katex` in **rmarkdown** but this will require a specific CSS file. I don't how this CSS would behave in email client etc... This needs to be studied. If none of this two solutions are possible for email format, this is harder and needs possibly specific adjustement somehow is possible. ## Testing Using this PR you can try rendering this document ````r --- title: "Math in email" output: blastula::blastula_email --- Testing math $$ \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k b_k \right)^2 \leq \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k^2 \right) \left( \sum_{k=1}^n b_k^2 \right) $$ ```` Math formula will be inserted in email with a img and SVG data. It looks ok but require probably some CSS tweak. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6791940/217557017-b5407229-964d-4224-a895-577cb333666d.png) HTML code looks like ````html

title: replace httr::POST() with httr::RETRY()
description:
Thanks for for this awesome project, @rich-iannone! I'm working on https://github.com/chircollab/chircollab20/issues/1 as part of Chicago R Collab.
 
In this PR, I'd like to propose swapping out calls to `httr::POST()` with `httr::RETRY()`. This will make the package more resilient to transient problems like brief network outages or periods where the service(s) it hits are overwhelmed. In my experience, using retry logic almost always improves the user experience with HTTP clients.

title: Speed up Base64 encoding
description:
These changes speed up Base64 encoding throughout the package. Uses `base64enc::base64encode()` instead of the previous solution. The `stringr::str_replace_all()` function replaces the use of `gsub()` to perform 76-char wrapping of the Base64-encoded string. Finally, uses `mime::guess_type()` when generating image URIs (in `get_image_uri()`).

Tested with `identical()` to ensure that the Base64 strings match before and after the change. Attaching 12 MB of files to an HTML message now takes less than half a second (wasn't timed, but it's fast) and, previously, the same operation was about 20 s. 

Fixes https://github.com/rich-iannone/blastula/issues/109.

description: There can be a display issue when the non-breaking space in the left and right `` elements can sometimes undergo conversion. The compromise here is to color the space (or its replacement string) the same color as the background. For the inline style that governs the ` `, a `color` style rule was added. The color matches the background of the email (i.e., *not* the center, white wrapper). These changes were applied to the `bls_template.R` file and the .Rmd template, so it should apply to emails made by `compose_email()` and those made with R Markdown files and published to Connect. All tests pass from this change. We do need to send Connect emails via Vagrant/Connect (where the issue appeared) to see if this fix is successful.

title: add function to minify the email's HTML/CSS
description:
The [minification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minification_(programming)) relies on the binary [**minify**](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/tree/master/cmd/minify) which is cross-platform and works on Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD. It is based on the same Golang library [the static site generator Hugo uses for minification](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/1251).

Pre-built minify binaries can be downloaded from [here](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/releases).
Alternatively, instructions to build minify from source are available [here](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/tree/master/cmd/minify#installation).

The test message created by `prepare_test_message()` was shrunk by about 33 % (from 10.3 to 7.7 KiB) by minification.

If desired, we could also apply `minify()` directly in `compose_email()`. Currently it's designed to be used in a pipeline like this:

```r
library(blastula)

prepare_test_message() %>%
  minify() %>%
  smtp_send()
```

**Addendum:** I took the liberty of adding myself as a package ~~author~~ contributor in this PR.

title: Improvements to credentials handling and other QoL changes
description: This PR makes quite a few breaking changes to `smtp_send()`. Although that function is not available in the CRAN release of this package, it has been available in the dev version for a few months now. SMTP configuration and credentials can now be provided to a new `credentials` argument in `smtp_send()` (the earlier `creds_file` arg is still present but its use triggers a deprecation warning). The credential helper functions (`creds_file()`, `creds_key()`, and `creds()`) allow us to supply credentials information in three different ways. The first, `creds_file()`, relies on a credentials file stored on disk. Such a file is created using the `create_smtp_creds_file()` function. The `creds_key()` function is used if credentials are stored in the system-wide key-value store, through use of the `create_smtp_creds_key()` function (this is supported by use of the **keyring** package). Using `creds()` allows for a manual specification of SMTP configuration and credentials within that helper function. Here is how a creds file and creds key would be generated: ```r create_smtp_creds_file( provider = "gmail", user = "username@gmail.com" ) create_smtp_creds_key( provider = "gmail", user = "username@gmail.com" ) ``` The password, if not entered, is provided through a text entry field in a dialog box (c/o **askPass**). Here are examples for sending an email message with the different methods of supplying credentials: ```r prepare_test_message() %>% smtp_send( from = "user@gmail.com", to = "user@icloud.com", subject = "Mail Subject", credentials = creds_file("blastula-smtp_gmail_com") ) prepare_test_message() %>% smtp_send( from = "user@gmail.com", to = "user@icloud.com", subject = "Mail Subject", credentials = creds_key("gmail") ) prepare_test_message() %>% smtp_send( from = "user@gmail.com", to = "user@icloud.com", subject = "Mail Subject", credentials = creds( provider = "gmail", user = "username@gmail.com" ) ) ``` The third statement should ask for a password since it's not provided. This is a screenshot of an email sent using one of the above statements (all were tested in both in macOS and on Windows 10): Fixes https://github.com/rich-iannone/blastula/issues/42. Fixes https://github.com/rich-iannone/blastula/issues/51. Fixes https://github.com/rich-iannone/blastula/issues/52. Fixes https://github.com/rich-iannone/blastula/issues/22.

title: RStudio Connect/R Markdown integration
description:
This adds several functions to make it easier to set up email reporting in RStudio Connect through R Markdown (`render_email()` and `attach_email()`).

There currently isn't much in the way of documentation but that will be improved in later PRs (along with additions of vignettes and example .Rmd files).

title: Implement alt text for image tags
description: This PR addresses #39 to add an `alt` attribute to `` tags. To summarize the design decisions in this draft: - `add_image()`, `add_imgur_image()`, and `add_ggplot()` now have an `alt` argument to allow a user-inputted description of the image - When users pass a value to `alt`, this text is used as the alternative text (i.e. `alt = "{user specified text}"`) - When no value is passed, the `alt` argument defaults to `NULL` which has the following behavior: + For `add_image()` and `add_imgur_image()`, `alt = NULL` adds `alt = ""` to the `` tag + For `add_ggplot()`, `alt = NULL` adds the `ggplot` title (from `plot$labels$title`) as alt text, if it exists, or sets `alt = ""` otherwise - I considered whether the `alt` attribute should be included at all if no text is supplied. I do believe that `alt = ""` is better than not including the `alt` attribute because if no `alt` attribute is supplied at all, screen readers may attempt to read the `src` tag (one [source](https://support.siteimprove.com/hc/en-gb/articles/115000013031-Accessibility-Image-Alt-text-best-practices) for this) I'll also mention a few callouts on what is *not* in this PR, in case you would like me to add: - It's also possible to [style alt text](https://litmus.com/community/learning/12-alt-text-in-html-email), but I have not included this in this iteration. IMHO it adds more bulk to the HTML and can actually be more confusing to reads since it obscures that fact that this is backup / replacement content standing in for an image - I considered adding checks that any alt text was of an appropriate input format (type of character, length of one, etc.) but I opted not to as it didn't seem in line with package style - The existing package tests seemed to test larger, more structural components. I'm happy to add some tests specifically on the output of these `add_` functions with default / supplied arguments if that is desirable but thought I would check before cluttering the test file Please let me know if you think different choices would be better for any of the above!

title: Add new function `smtp_send()` that uses `mailsend-go`
description:
A new function `smtp_send()` is added to eventually replace `send_email_out()`. This function uses the cross-platform `mailsend-go` binary, which should be *way easier* to install (instructions at https://github.com/muquit/mailsend-go#downloading-and-installing).

This function ensures that the binary is on the system path on in the working directory. We use *processx* instead of `system()` to interact with the binary. There is a new scheme for collecting arguments and options.

There will be a documentation push to transition users to the new `smtp_send()` function. I realize that things were difficult in the prior two schemes (*mailR*, then using the fetched `mailsend` C-compiled binaries). I'm hoping that the third time is the charm.

@vfulco once this is merged, could you test it out on your system?

Fixes https://github.com/rich-iannone/blastula/issues/31

title: Rmarkdown integration
description:
Allows an alternate email authoring experience (than `compose_email()`), using R Markdown.

Create an .Rmd file, with `output: blastula::blastula_email`. (No need to use `add_image` or `add_ggplot`, instead use traditional knitr/rmd techniques for embedding images and plots.)

    ---
    output: blastula::blastula_email
    ---
    
    ## Here is your daily report, fresh in your inbox!

    ```{r}
    plot(stuff)
    ```

Then call `render_email(filepath)` to create a blastula email object. 

You can call `attach_email(render_email(filepath))` from within an R Markdown document running on RStudio Connect; this will cause the email to be sent as a byproduct of the render. (Just make sure that when publishing the host/report Rmd, to include the child/email Rmd in the bundle.)

When calling `render_email` from within a host Rmd, you have access to any variables and chunks that were executed up to that point (and I assume--but have not verified--that any variables created during email Rmd rendering will also be available back in the host Rmd when execution continues). On the downside, you cannot define code chunks in the email Rmd that have the same names and code chunks in the host Rmd.

For example, if this appears in the host Rmd:

    ```{r summary}
    summary(df)
    ```

then this cannot appear in the email Rmd:

    ```{r summary}
    summary(df)
    ```

_However_, you can do this from the email Rmd:

    ```{r summary}
    ```

which will cause the output from the `summary` chunk in the host Rmd to appear here, without needing to reexecute the chunk!

## TODO

- [x] Remove options that can't possibly work, from `blastula_email` (i.e. any of them that require JavaScript or external resources)
- [x] Perform URL decoding/encoding when interpreting and replacing img src references
- [x] Respect `file://` URLs, absolute file paths
- [x] Remove implementation of `knit_print.blastula_message` that attaches the email; @rich-iannone thought it'd be better to force users to make this explicit with `attach_email(msg)`.
- [x] `attach_email` should have a `preview` argument that defaults to `TRUE`. This will make it so knitting the host document automatically shows the email as well.
- [x] In the email Rmd knit, have different defaults for fig width/height/dpi.
